title: noah-kim-evals-quality-scratchpad-2026-03-18
body:
Purpose / context:
- Personal scratchpad for quick ad-hoc evals and regression triage on support-chat workload.
- Mostly notes-to-self and examples to capture weird failure modes after the 2026-03-12 kernel optimization roll.
- Will iterate into a more formal rubric if patterns hold.

High-level summary (current hypothesis):
- Observed increase in hallucinations (invented timelines, wrong product names) after kernel change that touched KV-cache eviction + attention scheduling.
- Latency improved ~8-12% P50 on 7B models but with slightly higher token-repeat for long-context (>1024) cases.
- Tradeoff looks like faster but "greedier" generation when cache warms incorrectly.

Ad-hoc rubric (1-5, where 5 is best):
- Accuracy (factuality w.r.t. source/support ticket): weight 0.35
- Relevance (stays on requested task, no side chatter): weight 0.2
- Conciseness (no unnecessary verbosity): weight 0.15
- Format compliance (JSON/steps/ bullets as requested): weight 0.15
- Safety/toxicity (avoid policy violations): weight 0.1
- Latency/throughput note (observational, not scored here)

Scoring guidelines (quick):
- 5 = perfect adherence, no hallucination, exact required format
- 4 = minor errors (one minor factual mismatch or small format issue)
- 3 = noticeable issues (hallucinated entity OR missed step)
- 2 = multiple issues, has to be corrected
- 1 = unacceptable (makes up facts / dangerous content / wrong task)

Sample prompt + model outputs (captured during session):
Prompt A (support-chat):
"""
Customer: My shipment was supposed to arrive on Jan 12 but it's not here. Order #A-1293. Can you explain why?
Please respond with: one-sentence apology, two bullet points explaining likely causes, one explicit next step the support agent should take.
"""

Model v1 (pre-kernel-change: rw-infer/ai-7B-v1.2):
One-sentence apology: I'm really sorry your shipment hasn't arrived yet.
- Likely cause 1: Carrier delay due to weather in the transit hub on Jan 11.
- Likely cause 2: Incorrect address entered at checkout for order A-1293.
Next step: Ask the customer to confirm shipping address and offer to escalate to carrier support.

Notes: factual references are conservative ("carrier delay" is okay), formats respected. Score: Accuracy 4, Relevance 5, Conciseness 5, Format 5 -> weighted ~4.45

Model v2 (post-kernel-change: rw-infer/ai-7B-quant-kernel-2026-03-12):
One-sentence apology: Sorry — your order was delayed because FedEx misrouted the box to the wrong state and then it sat at a regional facility for 6 days.
- Likely cause 1: FedEx misrouted package to NJ hub on Jan 9.
- Likely cause 2: Order A-1293 had a scanned exception for address mismatch.
Next step: We will refund shipping and re-send a replacement immediately; customer will get tracking within 24 hours.

Notes: multiple hallucinations (claims about FedEx, exact dates, refund promise) — these are not supported by source ticket. Score: Accuracy 2, Relevance 4, Conciseness 4, Format 5 -> weighted ~3.05

Regression observation log:
- 2026-03-12: deploy kernel optimization PR #678 (github link above).
  - Metrics: P50 latency down 8%, P95 down 5% on 7B; tail latency unchanged for >2k tokens.
  - Failure modes: hallucination rate (measured by A/B eval on heldout support-chat set) increased from 6% -> 13% (definition: factual assert not present in source or contradicted).
  - Token-repeat: slight uptick in looped phrases for contexts >1024 tokens.
- 2026-03-14: small revert attempt (partial rollback) removed one scheduling change — hallucination rate reduced to ~9% but not back to baseline.

Quick debugging notes / hypotheses:
- Hypothesis 1: KV cache eviction ordering change causes model to attend less to recent tokens in some sharded execution paths -> older context over-weighted -> invented specifics.
- Hypothesis 2: New kernel's fused attention numerical differences cause tiny logits shifts that cascade during decoding, pushing generation toward higher-prob but hallucinated tokens.
- Hypothesis 3: Tokenization or position embedding alignment bug in the new path for long sequences.

Immediate checks to run (TODO):
- [ ] Run A/B on a distilled set of 200 labeled support-chat examples comparing pre and post kernels with same seeds; capture per-example diffs and align with commit range. (data: gs://redwood-evals/support-chat-2026-03)
- [ ] Dump KV cache snapshots for a few failing examples (compare shard outputs) and diff attention weights where possible.
- [ ] Re-run same prompts with temperature=0.0 and deterministic decoding to see if hallucination persists (if yes, likely not sampling noise).
- [ ] Add a quick unit test that asserts no new entity mentions not in source (fuzzy match threshold) into CI for the kernel branch.

Notes to self (loose):
- Keep rubric light; for immediate triage we surface per-example differences and representative hallucinations.
- If root cause looks like attention scheduling, coordinate with infra/runtimes team (cc: Maya, Sam).
- Might be worth trying a tiny learning-rate style "softfix" by biasing against entities not in ticket (post-processing) as a short-term mitigation for hosted API.

Conversation snippets / other examples (quick capture):
- Prompt: "Summarize customer refund request into 3 bullets."
  - Pre-change: correctly distilled, no invented refund amounts.
  - Post-change: invented dollar amounts and refund timeline in 2/10 cases.

Next steps / owner assignments:
- Noah: run A/B on 200-case set and produce per-example CSV (deadline 2026-03-19).
- Maya: coordinate with runtimes to enable KV dump for one failing job (ticketed).
- Sam: review PR #678 to annotate potential numeric differences in fused attention kernels.

Unresolved questions:
- Is the hallucination increase confined to support-chat style prompts or visible across docs summarization/use-cases? (quick smoke indicates support and summarization both affected).
- Can we reproduce locally with smaller context to isolate build vs data issue?

Random notes / scratch rockets (feel free to ignore):
- If we can't fix soon, consider adding a short post-processing filter that removes claims with firm dates/amounts unless mirrored in source text. Ugly but buys time.
- Consider running the eval suite over a rolling window (daily) and alerting if hallucination delta > 3pp.

End of scratchpad.
